item.title: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!: Re: 9th Annual Holiday Art Exchange~!
item.content:encoded:
Okay, this is probably the first one of these I actually have time for, so I might as well put my name down.

What I can give: I can write SCPs or tales, although I'm better at the former. I lean towards concept-driven articles rather than sappy emotional stories. I'm also a cellist, for what that's worth.

What I am looking for: I will take art or an article featuring any of my solo SCPs (SCP-2801, SCP-3631, or SCP-4943), but I would especially like an article featuring my home-grown GOI Ravensgate Security Services. The short version is that they are a security firm that does pentesting, consulting, etc. for other GOIs, including the Foundation. I don't expect them to get very big - they are admittedly very niche - but I do want to flesh them out. For characters, you could include David Keyes's team, or you could write your own. The organizational structure isn't very well defined so far, so you have some freedom on that front. All I ask is that they remain a benevolent force, or at least a neutral one.

item.title: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France: Re: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5245 consists of a ceramic mask with blank eyes and a wide smile, in addition to a black substance which is, at rest, the consistency of a borax-glue “slime” mixture, though 5245 can change this consistency at will. The amount of this substance varies proportional to feeding habits, though 5245 claims to be uncomfortable with less than 10.7 liters of fluid, and should thus be maintained above that. Amounts less than 750ml of the substance can be separated from SCP-5245 with no ill effects, and is not physically active, though SCP-5245 can still feel when it’s touched and control its viscosity.This substance will turn into unglazed ceramic after approximately 1 hour if not reconstituted into 5245.

Deleted at -14 and three votes.

SCP-5083 is a standard black universal tv remote measuring 2 inches in width and 7.5 inches in length. Despite SCP-5083 being a tv remote, it has no observable space to insert batteries. Each button on SCP-5038 seemingly has a different effect on reality but can be made to affect one specific item or individual by pointing SCP-5083 at the target and pressing a button.

Deleted at -23 and three votes.

Held at Site ██, SCP-5133 is an anomalous entity resembling the remains of an unknown male who has suffered from Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The Being is capable of decaying and disintegration objects (including other beings) that it touches. The effect of this disintegration becomes stronger and faster the longer the object is held. SCP-5133's origin is currently unknown as well as the age of it. SCP-5133 is 184 centimeters tall and weighs approximately 15kg.

Deleted at -19 and three votes.

SCP-5487 is located in █████, United States. SCP-5487 resembles a Dell Dimension 4500, but it has 2 extra oddly shaped ports at the back. The first of these ports is connected by wire to a mahogany door frame, although no door is present within the frame. The second is connected to what appears to be a large scanner, about 2ft x 2ft.

Deleted at -15 and three votes.

item.title: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France: Re: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France
item.content:encoded:
Deleted an article by TheBeginningIsTheEnd at -15 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description:
SCP-5127 is a parasite that attaches itself to it's victims through ingestion of SCP-5127.
It manifests as a purple mold usually found on items such as fresh vegetables and fruits.
It can multiply and spread throughout entire farms in mere minutes, as it has been enhanced by unknown means to find the quickest way to infect a human body.

Feedback is as follows:

+ Ralliston
– Ralliston

Author, the mainsite is for finished works. This is clearly not finished - it’s lacking an Object Class and Special Containment Procedures. Additionally, this reads a lot like a generic thing which kills you. I suggest you use the ideas critique forums to polish the idea up to give it some depth, the place can be of great help.

Also,

D-Class Test Results
378 D-Class personnel have ingested SCP-5127, each with results varying inbetween the above side-effects.

I highly doubt the Foundation would sacrifice 387 people on such tests.

+ TSATPWTCOTTTADC
– TSATPWTCOTTTADC

Author, take a look at the instructions on the How to Write and SCP guide linked in the sidebar to learn how to give your article a title the right way.

Deleted an article by Agent malcom at -15 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5729 is a cancerous growth located in the upper abdominal area and in 5% of cases brain working as a separate organ, which upon being "activated" by an unknown factor it will manifest into rapid growths forming any of the following: controlable tentacle-like structures, coverage of the arms and/or legs or a violent burst. Upon activation of SCP-5729 the subject from now on named SCP-5729-1 will become highly aggresive attacking every multi-celular organism it encounters.

Feedback is as follows:

+ ItsDenali
– ItsDenali

This feels really short and underdeveloped, and the second breach log being almost entirely redacted doesn't add anything to the article as a whole. Really all you've got here is a thing that does a thing, without much depth to it.

This idea does have potential, but I'd take this back to the Critique Forum and try to develop more points on it, such as what causes it, where it comes from, and what -1 instances' "common goal" is beyond escaping and killing people at random.

Good luck, author.

+ MrAnakinSpecter
– MrAnakinSpecter

Aside from the conceptual feedback (which I second) already given, I would like to add that you might also want to double-check some words if you aren't sure how to spell them, author. Additionally, what I'm assuming are supposed to be black boxes at the end are not showing up for me.

Deleted an article by Douglas Gorde at -13 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5315 is a horse barn found in ████, Michigan. Its dimensions equate to roughly 30’x40’x30’. It is constructed almost entirely from oak and has been painted red with white highlights on supports or moldings, though the paint has chipped and faded due to age. SCP-5315 contains a large, main door, a back door, and a window situated above the main door which could be used to access the loft.

Feedback is as follows:

+ MrAnakinSpecter
– MrAnakinSpecter

30’x40’x30’.

Use metric.

If the main door of SCO-5315

SCP*

This isn't a terrible concept, but I think that the pure descriptive nature of the writing takes away any sort intrigue added by the anomaly.

item.content:encoded:
Deleted an article by Cole 13 at -20 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5127-J is a translucent ghost version of Michael Gary Scott, the branch manager of Dunder Mifflin Scranton SCP-5127-J first appeared when Steve Carell finished The Office in 2011. Before the foundation knew anything about SCP-5127-J, It was roaming Steve Carell's mansion. After Steve Carrel said anything, SCP-5127-J responded with "That's what she said" which made anything Steve said seem wrong. It happened so frequently, Steve Carrel began to lose money from low self esteem and stress. The foundation kept his losses under wraps as they would eventually ruin his career. He wrote letters to the producers and begged them to let him back on to the show. Eventually in the last episode, They let him back in. For a while during the recording, SCP-5127-J was silent. But when they aired the episode, SCP-5127-J came back. The first instance after the show was when Steve was cleaning up after the family meal and he said," I'm going to put this back." and SCP-5127-J responded," That's what she said." Recently the foundation has recorded 600,000 USD that Steve Carrel has lost to SCP-5127-J.

No feedback present.

item.title: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France: Re: Deletions 69: the seventh most populous urban area in France
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5234 is a 3 m x 1.5 m white shower curtain, with simple striped patterns, and bears signs of considerable use, molding, and age. It can emit a noise that closely resembles soft and faint whispers. Subjects within a 10 m radius of SCP-5234 that hear the whispers undergo a hypnotic and frenzied state.1 If SCP-5234 comes into contact with skin or any exposed part of the body, the person in question who has made initial contact with SCP-5234 is to be marked as SCP-5234-A. While the appendage or limb that’s stuck is to be amputated immediately. Salvaging as much as possible off of SCP-5234 to avoid the further feeding and development of SCP-5234. If the torso, head, and or more than three appendages are stuck to SCP-5234, then an immediate termination of SCP-5234-A is put into effect. Alongside the salvaging and cremation of any leftover body parts stuck to SCP-5234. After a period of one (1) to three (3) days, if SCP-5234-A hasn’t freed themselves from contact (or died from natural causes) The following anomalies' effects will begin to take place.

Deleted at -18 and three votes.

SCP-5083 is a 1.6 x 2.1 meter elevator and 2 x 30 meter elevator shaft. The elevator is comprised of steel and has seven buttons on the inside of it. The shaft however, is comprised of steel and an unknown substance. SCP-5083 functions as a normal elevator but when button seven is pressed the person(s) inside the elevator will be taken to the place they subconsciously most desire. This function is automatic and does not require user input. Places recorded have been The Fiji Islands, low Earth orbit, and England. In all instances, the elevator returns within 20 minutes after leaving the facility area.

Deleted at -18 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

ManyMeats

+ show block
– hide block

Hello author.

I downvoted this article largely because you attempt to deliver all of your emotion purely through telling. Your logs repeatedly describe Dr. Spencer's growing frustration and sadness at his situation but this is contained -entirely- within diary entries where the doctor says "I am more frustrated".

There is no emotion at all to attach myself to as a reader. Even if the motives and conclusion make sense, I feel no cause or need to act behind it all.
